about: Which of CUAD's 41 categories are risks our review is supposed to surface, and what
our review calls them. Curated by hand: CUAD annotates clauses a lawyer should read
in a corporate transaction, which is a wider question than 'what exposes our client'.
risky=false is not 'harmless'. It means the category is either metadata (who signed,
when it starts) or an annotation whose riskiness depends on terms CUAD does not
record, so counting a miss against the review would be measuring the benchmark's
framing rather than the review's judgement. Layer 1b's recall denominator is the
high_stakes=true sends a judge verdict to a human however confident the judge was.
'names' are the words our prompts and our reviewers use for the same clause; they
are documentation, not matching keys — span matching is Jaccard over text.
Missing on purpose: indemnities. CUAD v1 has no indemnity category, so the review's
indemnity findings land in off_benchmark_findings and no recall number covers them.
testingDocs/expected.json does cover indemnities, which is part of why the fixture
suite is not redundant with this one.

Uncapped Liability.note: The single worst thing in a commercial contract; critical severity if it is one-sided.

Cap On Liability.note: Risky as an asymmetry: a cap on their side beside none on ours is the finding.

Liquidated Damages.note: A pre-agreed number that bypasses proof of loss.

Ip Ownership Assignment.note: Who owns what was made, and whether the client's own materials went with it.

Joint Ip Ownership.note: Joint ownership is rarely what either side wanted and is hard to exploit.

Irrevocable Or Perpetual License.note: A grant that cannot be taken back, including after termination.

Unlimited/All-You-Can-Eat-License.note: Unmetered use of something that was priced per seat or per unit.

Non-Transferable License.note: Blocks a reorganisation or a sale of the business that relies on the licence.

Termination For Convenience.note: Risky as an asymmetry: their right to walk beside our obligation to stay.

Post-Termination Services.note: Work that outlives the contract, sometimes unpriced.

Renewal Term.note: Rolls the term over unless someone remembers to act.

Notice Period To Terminate Renewal.note: A long window is how an auto-renewal becomes a multi-year commitment.

Non-Compete.note: Restrains our own business, often past termination.

Exclusivity.note: Forecloses every other supplier or channel.

No-Solicit Of Customers.note: Limits who we may sell to after the deal.

No-Solicit Of Employees.note: Limits hiring; watch for it covering people who approach us unprompted.

Non-Disparagement.note: Restrains speech, including honest public comment.

Anti-Assignment.note: Risky as an asymmetry, and a blocker in any sale of the business.

Change Of Control.note: Lets the counterparty react to our own acquisition.

Rofr/Rofo/Rofn.note: Constrains a future transaction before it is contemplated.

Most Favored Nation.note: Ties every other customer's price to this one.

Minimum Commitment.note: Spend owed whether or not it is used.

Volume Restriction.note: Caps how much we may buy or sell.

Price Restrictions.note: A unilateral right to change the price is the usual shape.

Revenue/Profit Sharing.note: An ongoing claim on our revenue.

Audit Rights.note: Access to our records and premises, sometimes at our cost.

Source Code Escrow.note: Relevant when absent as well as present; CUAD only annotates present.

Third Party Beneficiary.note: Someone who did not sign can enforce against us.

Document Name.note: Metadata. The review summarises the document; it does not flag its title.

Expiration Date.note: Metadata. The term's length is a risk; the date it ends is not.

Governing Law.note: Which law applies is metadata. A governing law left blank is a risk, and CUAD has no annotation for an absent clause, so the review cannot be scored on it here.

License Grant.note: Every licence agreement has one; the risk is in its scope, which the narrower licence categories cover.

Affiliate License-Licensor.note: Scope detail. Risky only in combination with terms CUAD does not annotate.

Competitive Restriction Exception.note: An exception that reduces a restriction. Flagging it as a risk would be wrong.

Insurance.note: An obligation whose weight is the required limits, which CUAD's span does not isolate.

Warranty Duration.note: A short warranty is a risk and a long one is not; the annotation does not say which.
